# pr-1453: gh-1444 [GOAL] iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth

## Description

Closes #1444
### What changed
Made the mobile sandbox fail loudly instead of silently (gh-1444): skill reads resolve `.pointer` files transparently, every swallowed network request renders a structured `[bridge]` error, secret presence is verifiable (`NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT`), and timeout results tell the truth.

- **AC1 (pointer reads):** `read .fah/skills/<n>/SKILL.md` follows the sibling `.pointer` to the compiled-in body via a new pure `skill_pointer.dart` resolver — wired into the `read` tool (all hosts), a conditional `cat` seam on the WASI shell, and the web `MemoryShell` file seam. Only `builtin://skills/…` targets resolve; a foreign/corrupt pointer is refused loudly (E1). `builtin://` URIs are accepted as direct read operands.
- **AC2 (no silent empty):** a builtin-resource read that would return an empty payload fails with an error naming the resource id (E5) instead of a silent success.
- **AC3 (bridge loudness):** `bridge_errors.dart` renders `[bridge] GET api.github.com: connection reset (rid c…)` lines — the python HTTP bridge and the curl builtin surface them in the tool result **and** app.log; the bridge makes exactly one attempt (no auto-retry of non-idempotent verbs).
- **AC4 (secret presence):** `SecretsExecutionEnv` injects a names-only roster (`FA_SECRET_VARS`); the sandbox `env` builtin renders `NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT` — values never render; `revokeSecret` keeps the name visible as ABSENT (E3).
- **AC5 (honest timeouts):** bash timeout results render the real cap (never "unknown seconds"), carry the captured partial output, and no longer wear the "uncaught exception" hint; mobile WASI default timeout raised 30s → 120s; killed stages keep a 64 KiB output tail.
- **AC6 (codeload):** the GitHub host matrix (api/raw/codeload/objects.githubusercontent.com + the `curl -L codeload…/tar.gz` recipe) is documented in the mobile host profile (≤1000 chars guard kept); redirect-following curl verified by unit test.
- **AC7 (log hygiene):** normal WASI exit codes log as `_start exited (status N)`, not `_start error:` — error lines in app.log mean harness faults again.
- **AC8 (python noise):** the `Could not find platform dependent libraries` warning is filtered from captured stderr (`WasiPythonNoiseFilter`).
- **E2/E7:** a mid-body connection reset delivers the partial payload with a `[bridge] … after N bytes (truncated)` line and exit 18; responses are capped at 256 MiB with a quota error naming both byte counts (exit 63).

### Key decisions
- Pointer resolution is one pure module (`lib/src/skills/skill_pointer.dart`) shared by the read tool and both mobile shells — one behavior everywhere, unit-testable without WASM.
- `cat` stays a coreutils.wasm applet (the gh-1274/#1335 host-cwd projection is pinned at the WASM stage boundary); the shell dispatches to a Dart cat **only** when a pointer is actually in play (`_catNeedsPointerSeam`: `builtin://` operand, or a missing file whose `.pointer` sibling resolves — an existing file always wins).
- The presence roster rides the exec env (names only) — no new wire, shells stay decorator-agnostic.
- Fixed a self-introduced curl `-w` regression (`%{url_effective}` rendered empty after the loud-failure refactor) by passing the effective URL explicitly.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/tools test/env test/secrets test/agent
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/bridge_loud_failures_test.dart \
  test/builtin_skill_pointer_test.dart test/sandbox_registry_test.dart \
  test/memory_shell_test.dart test/wasm_shell_builtins_test.dart \
  test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart test/sandbox_secret_presence_test.dart \
  test/sandbox_curl_data_test.dart test/wasm_shell_host_cwd_test.dart
```

**Known pre-existing failures in this runner (not from this branch):** golden pixel tests (proven: `origin/main` fails them identically — font rasterization drift), `wasm_sandbox_toolchain_test` (no desktop `libwasm_run_dart.so` provisioned), `providers_queue_writer_io_test` + 6 `test/integration` e2e tests (the runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` env var; all 6 pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`). Simulator-only E2E legs (AC1 byte-identical on device, AC6 real codeload tarball, AC7 app.log spot-check) need an iOS simulator run.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  M[model] -->|read .fah/skills/n/SKILL.md| RT[read tool]
  RT --> SP[skill_pointer resolver]
  SP -->|builtin://skills target| EMB[compiled-in SKILL.md]
  SP -->|foreign target| ERR[loud refusal]
  M -->|bash cat / env| WS[WASI shell]
  WS -->|cat + pointer in play| SEAM[Dart cat seam]
  WS -->|plain cat| APP[coreutils.wasm applet]
  SEAM --> SP
  WS -->|python bridge / curl| BR[bridge_errors lines]
  BR --> TR[tool result stderr] & LOG[app.log bridge tag]
  SE[SecretsExecutionEnv roster] -->|FA_SECRET_VARS| WS
```

</details>

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1453
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1453
- **Title**: gh-1444 [GOAL] iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1444` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 35
- **Additions**: +2775
- **Deletions**: -148
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T14:04:39Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T18:21:25Z

## PR Description

Closes #1444
### What changed
Made the mobile sandbox fail loudly instead of silently (gh-1444): skill reads resolve `.pointer` files transparently, every swallowed network request renders a structured `[bridge]` error, secret presence is verifiable (`NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT`), and timeout results tell the truth.

- **AC1 (pointer reads):** `read .fah/skills/<n>/SKILL.md` follows the sibling `.pointer` to the compiled-in body via a new pure `skill_pointer.dart` resolver — wired into the `read` tool (all hosts), a conditional `cat` seam on the WASI shell, and the web `MemoryShell` file seam. Only `builtin://skills/…` targets resolve; a foreign/corrupt pointer is refused loudly (E1). `builtin://` URIs are accepted as direct read operands.
- **AC2 (no silent empty):** a builtin-resource read that would return an empty payload fails with an error naming the resource id (E5) instead of a silent success.
- **AC3 (bridge loudness):** `bridge_errors.dart` renders `[bridge] GET api.github.com: connection reset (rid c…)` lines — the python HTTP bridge and the curl builtin surface them in the tool result **and** app.log; the bridge makes exactly one attempt (no auto-retry of non-idempotent verbs).
- **AC4 (secret presence):** `SecretsExecutionEnv` injects a names-only roster (`FA_SECRET_VARS`); the sandbox `env` builtin renders `NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT` — values never render; `revokeSecret` keeps the name visible as ABSENT (E3).
- **AC5 (honest timeouts):** bash timeout results render the real cap (never "unknown seconds"), carry the captured partial output, and no longer wear the "uncaught exception" hint; mobile WASI default timeout raised 30s → 120s; killed stages keep a 64 KiB output tail.
- **AC6 (codeload):** the GitHub host matrix (api/raw/codeload/objects.githubusercontent.com + the `curl -L codeload…/tar.gz` recipe) is documented in the mobile host profile (≤1000 chars guard kept); redirect-following curl verified by unit test.
- **AC7 (log hygiene):** normal WASI exit codes log as `_start exited (status N)`, not `_start error:` — error lines in app.log mean harness faults again.
- **AC8 (python noise):** the `Could not find platform dependent libraries` warning is filtered from captured stderr (`WasiPythonNoiseFilter`).
- **E2/E7:** a mid-body connection reset delivers the partial payload with a `[bridge] … after N bytes (truncated)` line and exit 18; responses are capped at 256 MiB with a quota error naming both byte counts (exit 63).

### Key decisions
- Pointer resolution is one pure module (`lib/src/skills/skill_pointer.dart`) shared by the read tool and both mobile shells — one behavior everywhere, unit-testable without WASM.
- `cat` stays a coreutils.wasm applet (the gh-1274/#1335 host-cwd projection is pinned at the WASM stage boundary); the shell dispatches to a Dart cat **only** when a pointer is actually in play (`_catNeedsPointerSeam`: `builtin://` operand, or a missing file whose `.pointer` sibling resolves — an existing file always wins).
- The presence roster rides the exec env (names only) — no new wire, shells stay decorator-agnostic.
- Fixed a self-introduced curl `-w` regression (`%{url_effective}` rendered empty after the loud-failure refactor) by passing the effective URL explicitly.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/tools test/env test/secrets test/agent
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/bridge_loud_failures_test.dart \
  test/builtin_skill_pointer_test.dart test/sandbox_registry_test.dart \
  test/memory_shell_test.dart test/wasm_shell_builtins_test.dart \
  test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart test/sandbox_secret_presence_test.dart \
  test/sandbox_curl_data_test.dart test/wasm_shell_host_cwd_test.dart
```

**Known pre-existing failures in this runner (not from this branch):** golden pixel tests (proven: `origin/main` fails them identically — font rasterization drift), `wasm_sandbox_toolchain_test` (no desktop `libwasm_run_dart.so` provisioned), `providers_queue_writer_io_test` + 6 `test/integration` e2e tests (the runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` env var; all 6 pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`). Simulator-only E2E legs (AC1 byte-identical on device, AC6 real codeload tarball, AC7 app.log spot-check) need an iOS simulator run.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  M[model] -->|read .fah/skills/n/SKILL.md| RT[read tool]
  RT --> SP[skill_pointer resolver]
  SP -->|builtin://skills target| EMB[compiled-in SKILL.md]
  SP -->|foreign target| ERR[loud refusal]
  M -->|bash cat / env| WS[WASI shell]
  WS -->|cat + pointer in play| SEAM[Dart cat seam]
  WS -->|plain cat| APP[coreutils.wasm applet]
  SEAM --> SP
  WS -->|python bridge / curl| BR[bridge_errors lines]
  BR --> TR[tool result stderr] & LOG[app.log bridge tag]
  SE[SecretsExecutionEnv roster] -->|FA_SECRET_VARS| WS
```

</details>

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):
🚨 **BLOCKING** — two red CI gates plus a sandbox regression must be fixed before merge.

**Summary**: The PR delivers solid, well-tested work (skill-pointer seam, env secret-presence roster, loud bridge failures, noise filtering — 1267 core tests green locally), but (1) the Quality gate is red: the new `&& timeoutArg != null` guard makes an inner null-check dead code → 2 analyzer warnings (`dart analyze` exit 2 vs 0 on main, reproduced locally); (2) the Flutter app CRAP ratchet is red (new/changed uncovered branches exceed the pinned 30.0 threshold); (3) the new `cat` pointer-seam probe reads every operand with `File.readAsString()`, so `cat` of any binary file (a downloaded tarball/PNG) now throws an uncaught exception where the coreutils applet previously handled it.

- 💡 AC6 remains documentation + simulated-client only; the device/simulator leg is deferred (noted in the PR — keep gh-1444's C6 open until it runs).

**Next Steps**:
1. Drop the redundant inner `timeoutArg != null` check (one-line fix) → Quality gate green.
2. Binary-safe the cat probe (bounded `readAsBytes` prefix or `.pointer`-existence gate) + add a binary-`cat` test; re-measure CRAP and cover or descent-note the new branches per `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`.
3. Register the prompt's advertised secret-name roster (or note the limitation) so `env` can render `ABSENT`.

---

### Thread 8

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):
## All three blockers fixed (plus the IMPORTANT and SUGGESTION threads)

**1. Quality gate (analyzer warnings) — fixed.** The redundant inner `timeoutArg != null` check in `lib/src/tools/builtin_tools_bash.dart` (dead code under the new retry guard's promotion) is dropped — exactly the one-line fix proposed. `dart analyze lib test bin` exits 0 again (45 pre-existing info-level hints, 0 warnings/errors).

**2. Binary-`cat` sandbox regression — fixed.** `_catNeedsPointerSeam` no longer reads operands at all: an existence probe keeps every existing file (text OR binary) on the binary-safe coreutils applet path, and only a *missing* operand consults pointer machinery. The Dart `_catBuiltin` (seam path) reads operands byte-first and appends raw bytes, so a tarball beside a pointer seam is delivered instead of thrown out of `exec()`; the text-only `_readSandboxTextFollowPointers` helper is deleted. Covered by the requested flutter unit test (`cat` of a non-UTF-8 tarball through `WasiSandboxShell` — exit 0, never throws; reproduced RED first with the exact `FileSystemException: Failed to decode data using encoding 'utf-8'` this review reported).

**3. CRAP ratchet — re-measured after the cat-probe fix landed** (as the thread required): see the thread-3 reply for the ranked violators and the covering tests / descent outcome.

Also fixed in this round:

- **AC4 `NAME: ABSENT` (IMPORTANT thread):** the roster registers the *advertised* name list (boot values + `knownKeyNames`), and the Keys settings delete is wired as the production `revokeSecret` path (delete → ABSENT with the name visible, re-save → PRESENT; dotenv-only names untouched). Five new `AgentService.create`-level tests pin it.
- **IPv6 `bridgeHostOfAuthority` (SUGGESTION):** now parses through `Uri` (`http://[::1]:8080/x` → `::1`), with tests; a corrupt authority still renders instead of crashing the failure path.

**Noted, no action (as flagged):** desktop CLI `env` keeps printing raw values (real `/usr/bin/env`) next to the names-only roster line — cross-surface divergence, no new value leak; AC6's device/simulator leg (real codeload tarball) stays deferred with gh-1444's C6 open until it runs.

---


## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

🚨 **BLOCKING: New analyzer warnings — `dart analyze` gate is red**

Adding `&& timeoutArg != null` to the retry guard promotes `timeoutArg` to non-null inside the block, which turns the pre-existing interpolation check below into dead code:

```dart
if (error.code == ExecutionErrorCode.timeout &&
    canRetry &&
    timeoutArg != null) {          // <- promotion happens here
  notices.add(
    '[bash attempt ... timed out'
    '${timeoutArg != null ? ' after ${timeoutArg}s' : ''} — '   // <- always true → warning + dead `: ''` branch
```

Reproduced locally: `dart analyze lib test bin` exits **2** on this branch (2 warnings: `unnecessary_null_comparison` + `dead_code` at `builtin_tools_bash.dart:375`) vs exit **0** on `origin/main`. This is the root cause of the failing **Quality gate** CI check.

Fix — the inner check is redundant under the new guard:

```dart
'[bash attempt $attempt/${bashToolMaxRetries + 1} timed out'
' after ${timeoutArg}s — '
'retrying]',
```

(The `throw _bashFailureError(error, notices, timeoutArg)` below is outside the guard and correctly still handles null.)

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `cat` of a binary file now throws an uncaught exception (mobile sandbox regression)**

`_catNeedsPointerSeam` eagerly calls `_readSandboxText(path)` — a full `File.readAsString()` — for **every** non-flag operand of **every** `cat` invocation, before the coreutils applet runs:

```dart
for (final path in args.where((a) => !a.startsWith('-'))) {
  if (await _readSandboxText(path) != null) continue;
```

`readAsString()` throws (`FileSystemException: Failed to decode data using encoding 'utf-8'`) on any non-UTF-8 content — a downloaded tarball, PNG, gzip blob. That exception escapes `_runStage` → `runShellScript` → `exec()`. The `Shell` contract returns `Result`, callers don't expect throws, so the tool surfaces an "uncaught exception inside the harness" error for a command that worked before this PR (the coreutils.wasm applet is binary-safe). This is exactly the file class AC6's own recipe produces (`curl -L ... codeload.github.com/.../tar.gz/...`).

Two additional costs even for valid text: every seamed `cat` reads the file **twice** (probe + applet), and the probe reads the *whole* file just to check for a pointer.

Suggested fix:

1. Probe cheaply and binary-safely: read a bounded prefix via `file.readAsBytes()` (e.g. first 4 KiB), treat `utf8.decode(prefix, allowMalformed: true)` losslessness (or a NUL-byte sniff) as the text test — or gate the probe on the existence of a `<path>.pointer` sibling via `File.exists()` instead of reading the operand at all.
2. Decide the binary path deliberately: with no pointer, let the applet handle the operand (pre-PR behavior) instead of routing bytes through a UTF-8 text API — both here and in `_catBuiltin`'s `_readSandboxTextFollowPointers` fallback, which has the same throw on binary operands.

Please add a flutter unit test: `cat` of a non-UTF-8 file through `WasiSandboxShell` returns the bytes/exit 0 and never throws.

blocks.text:
# pr-1453: gh-1444 [GOAL] iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth

## Description

Closes #1444
### What changed
Made the mobile sandbox fail loudly instead of silently (gh-1444): skill reads resolve `.pointer` files transparently, every swallowed network request renders a structured `[bridge]` error, secret presence is verifiable (`NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT`), and timeout results tell the truth.

- **AC1 (pointer reads):** `read .fah/skills/<n>/SKILL.md` follows the sibling `.pointer` to the compiled-in body via a new pure `skill_pointer.dart` resolver — wired into the `read` tool (all hosts), a conditional `cat` seam on the WASI shell, and the web `MemoryShell` file seam. Only `builtin://skills/…` targets resolve; a foreign/corrupt pointer is refused loudly (E1). `builtin://` URIs are accepted as direct read operands.
- **AC2 (no silent empty):** a builtin-resource read that would return an empty payload fails with an error naming the resource id (E5) instead of a silent success.
- **AC3 (bridge loudness):** `bridge_errors.dart` renders `[bridge] GET api.github.com: connection reset (rid c…)` lines — the python HTTP bridge and the curl builtin surface them in the tool result **and** app.log; the bridge makes exactly one attempt (no auto-retry of non-idempotent verbs).
- **AC4 (secret presence):** `SecretsExecutionEnv` injects a names-only roster (`FA_SECRET_VARS`); the sandbox `env` builtin renders `NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT` — values never render; `revokeSecret` keeps the name visible as ABSENT (E3).
- **AC5 (honest timeouts):** bash timeout results render the real cap (never "unknown seconds"), carry the captured partial output, and no longer wear the "uncaught exception" hint; mobile WASI default timeout raised 30s → 120s; killed stages keep a 64 KiB output tail.
- **AC6 (codeload):** the GitHub host matrix (api/raw/codeload/objects.githubusercontent.com + the `curl -L codeload…/tar.gz` recipe) is documented in the mobile host profile (≤1000 chars guard kept); redirect-following curl verified by unit test.
- **AC7 (log hygiene):** normal WASI exit codes log as `_start exited (status N)`, not `_start error:` — error lines in app.log mean harness faults again.
- **AC8 (python noise):** the `Could not find platform dependent libraries` warning is filtered from captured stderr (`WasiPythonNoiseFilter`).
- **E2/E7:** a mid-body connection reset delivers the partial payload with a `[bridge] … after N bytes (truncated)` line and exit 18; responses are capped at 256 MiB with a quota error naming both byte counts (exit 63).

### Key decisions
- Pointer resolution is one pure module (`lib/src/skills/skill_pointer.dart`) shared by the read tool and both mobile shells — one behavior everywhere, unit-testable without WASM.
- `cat` stays a coreutils.wasm applet (the gh-1274/#1335 host-cwd projection is pinned at the WASM stage boundary); the shell dispatches to a Dart cat **only** when a pointer is actually in play (`_catNeedsPointerSeam`: `builtin://` operand, or a missing file whose `.pointer` sibling resolves — an existing file always wins).
- The presence roster rides the exec env (names only) — no new wire, shells stay decorator-agnostic.
- Fixed a self-introduced curl `-w` regression (`%{url_effective}` rendered empty after the loud-failure refactor) by passing the effective URL explicitly.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/tools test/env test/secrets test/agent
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/bridge_loud_failures_test.dart \
  test/builtin_skill_pointer_test.dart test/sandbox_registry_test.dart \
  test/memory_shell_test.dart test/wasm_shell_builtins_test.dart \
  test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart test/sandbox_secret_presence_test.dart \
  test/sandbox_curl_data_test.dart test/wasm_shell_host_cwd_test.dart
```

**Known pre-existing failures in this runner (not from this branch):** golden pixel tests (proven: `origin/main` fails them identically — font rasterization drift), `wasm_sandbox_toolchain_test` (no desktop `libwasm_run_dart.so` provisioned), `providers_queue_writer_io_test` + 6 `test/integration` e2e tests (the runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` env var; all 6 pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`). Simulator-only E2E legs (AC1 byte-identical on device, AC6 real codeload tarball, AC7 app.log spot-check) need an iOS simulator run.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  M[model] -->|read .fah/skills/n/SKILL.md| RT[read tool]
  RT --> SP[skill_pointer resolver]
  SP -->|builtin://skills target| EMB[compiled-in SKILL.md]
  SP -->|foreign target| ERR[loud refusal]
  M -->|bash cat / env| WS[WASI shell]
  WS -->|cat + pointer in play| SEAM[Dart cat seam]
  WS -->|plain cat| APP[coreutils.wasm applet]
  SEAM --> SP
  WS -->|python bridge / curl| BR[bridge_errors lines]
  BR --> TR[tool result stderr] & LOG[app.log bridge tag]
  SE[SecretsExecutionEnv roster] -->|FA_SECRET_VARS| WS
```

</details>

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1453
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1453
- **Title**: gh-1444 [GOAL] iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1444` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 35
- **Additions**: +2775
- **Deletions**: -148
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T14:04:39Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T18:21:25Z

## PR Description

Closes #1444
### What changed
Made the mobile sandbox fail loudly instead of silently (gh-1444): skill reads resolve `.pointer` files transparently, every swallowed network request renders a structured `[bridge]` error, secret presence is verifiable (`NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT`), and timeout results tell the truth.

- **AC1 (pointer reads):** `read .fah/skills/<n>/SKILL.md` follows the sibling `.pointer` to the compiled-in body via a new pure `skill_pointer.dart` resolver — wired into the `read` tool (all hosts), a conditional `cat` seam on the WASI shell, and the web `MemoryShell` file seam. Only `builtin://skills/…` targets resolve; a foreign/corrupt pointer is refused loudly (E1). `builtin://` URIs are accepted as direct read operands.
- **AC2 (no silent empty):** a builtin-resource read that would return an empty payload fails with an error naming the resource id (E5) instead of a silent success.
- **AC3 (bridge loudness):** `bridge_errors.dart` renders `[bridge] GET api.github.com: connection reset (rid c…)` lines — the python HTTP bridge and the curl builtin surface them in the tool result **and** app.log; the bridge makes exactly one attempt (no auto-retry of non-idempotent verbs).
- **AC4 (secret presence):** `SecretsExecutionEnv` injects a names-only roster (`FA_SECRET_VARS`); the sandbox `env` builtin renders `NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT` — values never render; `revokeSecret` keeps the name visible as ABSENT (E3).
- **AC5 (honest timeouts):** bash timeout results render the real cap (never "unknown seconds"), carry the captured partial output, and no longer wear the "uncaught exception" hint; mobile WASI default timeout raised 30s → 120s; killed stages keep a 64 KiB output tail.
- **AC6 (codeload):** the GitHub host matrix (api/raw/codeload/objects.githubusercontent.com + the `curl -L codeload…/tar.gz` recipe) is documented in the mobile host profile (≤1000 chars guard kept); redirect-following curl verified by unit test.
- **AC7 (log hygiene):** normal WASI exit codes log as `_start exited (status N)`, not `_start error:` — error lines in app.log mean harness faults again.
- **AC8 (python noise):** the `Could not find platform dependent libraries` warning is filtered from captured stderr (`WasiPythonNoiseFilter`).
- **E2/E7:** a mid-body connection reset delivers the partial payload with a `[bridge] … after N bytes (truncated)` line and exit 18; responses are capped at 256 MiB with a quota error naming both byte counts (exit 63).

### Key decisions
- Pointer resolution is one pure module (`lib/src/skills/skill_pointer.dart`) shared by the read tool and both mobile shells — one behavior everywhere, unit-testable without WASM.
- `cat` stays a coreutils.wasm applet (the gh-1274/#1335 host-cwd projection is pinned at the WASM stage boundary); the shell dispatches to a Dart cat **only** when a pointer is actually in play (`_catNeedsPointerSeam`: `builtin://` operand, or a missing file whose `.pointer` sibling resolves — an existing file always wins).
- The presence roster rides the exec env (names only) — no new wire, shells stay decorator-agnostic.
- Fixed a self-introduced curl `-w` regression (`%{url_effective}` rendered empty after the loud-failure refactor) by passing the effective URL explicitly.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/tools test/env test/secrets test/agent
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/bridge_loud_failures_test.dart \
  test/builtin_skill_pointer_test.dart test/sandbox_registry_test.dart \
  test/memory_shell_test.dart test/wasm_shell_builtins_test.dart \
  test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart test/sandbox_secret_presence_test.dart \
  test/sandbox_curl_data_test.dart test/wasm_shell_host_cwd_test.dart
```

**Known pre-existing failures in this runner (not from this branch):** golden pixel tests (proven: `origin/main` fails them identically — font rasterization drift), `wasm_sandbox_toolchain_test` (no desktop `libwasm_run_dart.so` provisioned), `providers_queue_writer_io_test` + 6 `test/integration` e2e tests (the runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` env var; all 6 pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`). Simulator-only E2E legs (AC1 byte-identical on device, AC6 real codeload tarball, AC7 app.log spot-check) need an iOS simulator run.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  M[model] -->|read .fah/skills/n/SKILL.md| RT[read tool]
  RT --> SP[skill_pointer resolver]
  SP -->|builtin://skills target| EMB[compiled-in SKILL.md]
  SP -->|foreign target| ERR[loud refusal]
  M -->|bash cat / env| WS[WASI shell]
  WS -->|cat + pointer in play| SEAM[Dart cat seam]
  WS -->|plain cat| APP[coreutils.wasm applet]
  SEAM --> SP
  WS -->|python bridge / curl| BR[bridge_errors lines]
  BR --> TR[tool result stderr] & LOG[app.log bridge tag]
  SE[SecretsExecutionEnv roster] -->|FA_SECRET_VARS| WS
```

</details>

# pr-1453: gh-1444 [GOAL] iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth

## Description

Closes #1444
### What changed
Made the mobile sandbox fail loudly instead of silently (gh-1444): skill reads resolve `.pointer` files transparently, every swallowed network request renders a structured `[bridge]` error, secret presence is verifiable (`NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT`), and timeout results tell the truth.

- **AC1 (pointer reads):** `read .fah/skills/<n>/SKILL.md` follows the sibling `.pointer` to the compiled-in body via a new pure `skill_pointer.dart` resolver — wired into the `read` tool (all hosts), a conditional `cat` seam on the WASI shell, and the web `MemoryShell` file seam. Only `builtin://skills/…` targets resolve; a foreign/corrupt pointer is refused loudly (E1). `builtin://` URIs are accepted as direct read operands.
- **AC2 (no silent empty):** a builtin-resource read that would return an empty payload fails with an error naming the resource id (E5) instead of a silent success.
- **AC3 (bridge loudness):** `bridge_errors.dart` renders `[bridge] GET api.github.com: connection reset (rid c…)` lines — the python HTTP bridge and the curl builtin surface them in the tool result **and** app.log; the bridge makes exactly one attempt (no auto-retry of non-idempotent verbs).
- **AC4 (secret presence):** `SecretsExecutionEnv` injects a names-only roster (`FA_SECRET_VARS`); the sandbox `env` builtin renders `NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT` — values never render; `revokeSecret` keeps the name visible as ABSENT (E3).
- **AC5 (honest timeouts):** bash timeout results render the real cap (never "unknown seconds"), carry the captured partial output, and no longer wear the "uncaught exception" hint; mobile WASI default timeout raised 30s → 120s; killed stages keep a 64 KiB output tail.
- **AC6 (codeload):** the GitHub host matrix (api/raw/codeload/objects.githubusercontent.com + the `curl -L codeload…/tar.gz` recipe) is documented in the mobile host profile (≤1000 chars guard kept); redirect-following curl verified by unit test.
- **AC7 (log hygiene):** normal WASI exit codes log as `_start exited (status N)`, not `_start error:` — error lines in app.log mean harness faults again.
- **AC8 (python noise):** the `Could not find platform dependent libraries` warning is filtered from captured stderr (`WasiPythonNoiseFilter`).
- **E2/E7:** a mid-body connection reset delivers the partial payload with a `[bridge] … after N bytes (truncated)` line and exit 18; responses are capped at 256 MiB with a quota error naming both byte counts (exit 63).

### Key decisions
- Pointer resolution is one pure module (`lib/src/skills/skill_pointer.dart`) shared by the read tool and both mobile shells — one behavior everywhere, unit-testable without WASM.
- `cat` stays a coreutils.wasm applet (the gh-1274/#1335 host-cwd projection is pinned at the WASM stage boundary); the shell dispatches to a Dart cat **only** when a pointer is actually in play (`_catNeedsPointerSeam`: `builtin://` operand, or a missing file whose `.pointer` sibling resolves — an existing file always wins).
- The presence roster rides the exec env (names only) — no new wire, shells stay decorator-agnostic.
- Fixed a self-introduced curl `-w` regression (`%{url_effective}` rendered empty after the loud-failure refactor) by passing the effective URL explicitly.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/tools test/env test/secrets test/agent
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/bridge_loud_failures_test.dart \
  test/builtin_skill_pointer_test.dart test/sandbox_registry_test.dart \
  test/memory_shell_test.dart test/wasm_shell_builtins_test.dart \
  test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart test/sandbox_secret_presence_test.dart \
  test/sandbox_curl_data_test.dart test/wasm_shell_host_cwd_test.dart
```

**Known pre-existing failures in this runner (not from this branch):** golden pixel tests (proven: `origin/main` fails them identically — font rasterization drift), `wasm_sandbox_toolchain_test` (no desktop `libwasm_run_dart.so` provisioned), `providers_queue_writer_io_test` + 6 `test/integration` e2e tests (the runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` env var; all 6 pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`). Simulator-only E2E legs (AC1 byte-identical on device, AC6 real codeload tarball, AC7 app.log spot-check) need an iOS simulator run.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  M[model] -->|read .fah/skills/n/SKILL.md| RT[read tool]
  RT --> SP[skill_pointer resolver]
  SP -->|builtin://skills target| EMB[compiled-in SKILL.md]
  SP -->|foreign target| ERR[loud refusal]
  M -->|bash cat / env| WS[WASI shell]
  WS -->|cat + pointer in play| SEAM[Dart cat seam]
  WS -->|plain cat| APP[coreutils.wasm applet]
  SEAM --> SP
  WS -->|python bridge / curl| BR[bridge_errors lines]
  BR --> TR[tool result stderr] & LOG[app.log bridge tag]
  SE[SecretsExecutionEnv roster] -->|FA_SECRET_VARS| WS
```

</details>

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1453
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1453
- **Title**: gh-1444 [GOAL] iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1444` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 35
- **Additions**: +2775
- **Deletions**: -148
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T14:04:39Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T18:21:25Z

## PR Description

Closes #1444
### What changed
Made the mobile sandbox fail loudly instead of silently (gh-1444): skill reads resolve `.pointer` files transparently, every swallowed network request renders a structured `[bridge]` error, secret presence is verifiable (`NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT`), and timeout results tell the truth.

- **AC1 (pointer reads):** `read .fah/skills/<n>/SKILL.md` follows the sibling `.pointer` to the compiled-in body via a new pure `skill_pointer.dart` resolver — wired into the `read` tool (all hosts), a conditional `cat` seam on the WASI shell, and the web `MemoryShell` file seam. Only `builtin://skills/…` targets resolve; a foreign/corrupt pointer is refused loudly (E1). `builtin://` URIs are accepted as direct read operands.
- **AC2 (no silent empty):** a builtin-resource read that would return an empty payload fails with an error naming the resource id (E5) instead of a silent success.
- **AC3 (bridge loudness):** `bridge_errors.dart` renders `[bridge] GET api.github.com: connection reset (rid c…)` lines — the python HTTP bridge and the curl builtin surface them in the tool result **and** app.log; the bridge makes exactly one attempt (no auto-retry of non-idempotent verbs).
- **AC4 (secret presence):** `SecretsExecutionEnv` injects a names-only roster (`FA_SECRET_VARS`); the sandbox `env` builtin renders `NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT` — values never render; `revokeSecret` keeps the name visible as ABSENT (E3).
- **AC5 (honest timeouts):** bash timeout results render the real cap (never "unknown seconds"), carry the captured partial output, and no longer wear the "uncaught exception" hint; mobile WASI default timeout raised 30s → 120s; killed stages keep a 64 KiB output tail.
- **AC6 (codeload):** the GitHub host matrix (api/raw/codeload/objects.githubusercontent.com + the `curl -L codeload…/tar.gz` recipe) is documented in the mobile host profile (≤1000 chars guard kept); redirect-following curl verified by unit test.
- **AC7 (log hygiene):** normal WASI exit codes log as `_start exited (status N)`, not `_start error:` — error lines in app.log mean harness faults again.
- **AC8 (python noise):** the `Could not find platform dependent libraries` warning is filtered from captured stderr (`WasiPythonNoiseFilter`).
- **E2/E7:** a mid-body connection reset delivers the partial payload with a `[bridge] … after N bytes (truncated)` line and exit 18; responses are capped at 256 MiB with a quota error naming both byte counts (exit 63).

### Key decisions
- Pointer resolution is one pure module (`lib/src/skills/skill_pointer.dart`) shared by the read tool and both mobile shells — one behavior everywhere, unit-testable without WASM.
- `cat` stays a coreutils.wasm applet (the gh-1274/#1335 host-cwd projection is pinned at the WASM stage boundary); the shell dispatches to a Dart cat **only** when a pointer is actually in play (`_catNeedsPointerSeam`: `builtin://` operand, or a missing file whose `.pointer` sibling resolves — an existing file always wins).
- The presence roster rides the exec env (names only) — no new wire, shells stay decorator-agnostic.
- Fixed a self-introduced curl `-w` regression (`%{url_effective}` rendered empty after the loud-failure refactor) by passing the effective URL explicitly.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/tools test/env test/secrets test/agent
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/bridge_loud_failures_test.dart \
  test/builtin_skill_pointer_test.dart test/sandbox_registry_test.dart \
  test/memory_shell_test.dart test/wasm_shell_builtins_test.dart \
  test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart test/sandbox_secret_presence_test.dart \
  test/sandbox_curl_data_test.dart test/wasm_shell_host_cwd_test.dart
```

**Known pre-existing failures in this runner (not from this branch):** golden pixel tests (proven: `origin/main` fails them identically — font rasterization drift), `wasm_sandbox_toolchain_test` (no desktop `libwasm_run_dart.so` provisioned), `providers_queue_writer_io_test` + 6 `test/integration` e2e tests (the runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` env var; all 6 pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`). Simulator-only E2E legs (AC1 byte-identical on device, AC6 real codeload tarball, AC7 app.log spot-check) need an iOS simulator run.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  M[model] -->|read .fah/skills/n/SKILL.md| RT[read tool]
  RT --> SP[skill_pointer resolver]
  SP -->|builtin://skills target| EMB[compiled-in SKILL.md]
  SP -->|foreign target| ERR[loud refusal]
  M -->|bash cat / env| WS[WASI shell]
  WS -->|cat + pointer in play| SEAM[Dart cat seam]
  WS -->|plain cat| APP[coreutils.wasm applet]
  SEAM --> SP
  WS -->|python bridge / curl| BR[bridge_errors lines]
  BR --> TR[tool result stderr] & LOG[app.log bridge tag]
  SE[SecretsExecutionEnv roster] -->|FA_SECRET_VARS| WS
```

</details>

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

🚨 **BLOCKING: New analyzer warnings — `dart analyze` gate is red**

Adding `&& timeoutArg != null` to the retry guard promotes `timeoutArg` to non-null inside the block, which turns the pre-existing interpolation check below into dead code:

```dart
if (error.code == ExecutionErrorCode.timeout &&
    canRetry &&
    timeoutArg != null) {          // <- promotion happens here
  notices.add(
    '[bash attempt ... timed out'
    '${timeoutArg != null ? ' after ${timeoutArg}s' : ''} — '   // <- always true → warning + dead `: ''` branch
```

Reproduced locally: `dart analyze lib test bin` exits **2** on this branch (2 warnings: `unnecessary_null_comparison` + `dead_code` at `builtin_tools_bash.dart:375`) vs exit **0** on `origin/main`. This is the root cause of the failing **Quality gate** CI check.

Fix — the inner check is redundant under the new guard:

```dart
'[bash attempt $attempt/${bashToolMaxRetries + 1} timed out'
' after ${timeoutArg}s — '
'retrying]',
```

(The `throw _bashFailureError(error, notices, timeoutArg)` below is outside the guard and correctly still handles null.)

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `cat` of a binary file now throws an uncaught exception (mobile sandbox regression)**

`_catNeedsPointerSeam` eagerly calls `_readSandboxText(path)` — a full `File.readAsString()` — for **every** non-flag operand of **every** `cat` invocation, before the coreutils applet runs:

```dart
for (final path in args.where((a) => !a.startsWith('-'))) {
  if (await _readSandboxText(path) != null) continue;
```

`readAsString()` throws (`FileSystemException: Failed to decode data using encoding 'utf-8'`) on any non-UTF-8 content — a downloaded tarball, PNG, gzip blob. That exception escapes `_runStage` → `runShellScript` → `exec()`. The `Shell` contract returns `Result`, callers don't expect throws, so the tool surfaces an "uncaught exception inside the harness" error for a command that worked before this PR (the coreutils.wasm applet is binary-safe). This is exactly the file class AC6's own recipe produces (`curl -L ... codeload.github.com/.../tar.gz/...`).

Two additional costs even for valid text: every seamed `cat` reads the file **twice** (probe + applet), and the probe reads the *whole* file just to check for a pointer.

Suggested fix:

1. Probe cheaply and binary-safely: read a bounded prefix via `file.readAsBytes()` (e.g. first 4 KiB), treat `utf8.decode(prefix, allowMalformed: true)` losslessness (or a NUL-byte sniff) as the text test — or gate the probe on the existence of a `<path>.pointer` sibling via `File.exists()` instead of reading the operand at all.
2. Decide the binary path deliberately: with no pointer, let the applet handle the operand (pre-PR behavior) instead of routing bytes through a UTF-8 text API — both here and in `_catBuiltin`'s `_readSandboxTextFollowPointers` fallback, which has the same throw on binary operands.

blocks.text:
# pr-1453: gh-1444 [GOAL] iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth

## Description

Closes #1444
### What changed
Made the mobile sandbox fail loudly instead of silently (gh-1444): skill reads resolve `.pointer` files transparently, every swallowed network request renders a structured `[bridge]` error, secret presence is verifiable (`NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT`), and timeout results tell the truth.

- **AC1 (pointer reads):** `read .fah/skills/<n>/SKILL.md` follows the sibling `.pointer` to the compiled-in body via a new pure `skill_pointer.dart` resolver — wired into the `read` tool (all hosts), a conditional `cat` seam on the WASI shell, and the web `MemoryShell` file seam. Only `builtin://skills/…` targets resolve; a foreign/corrupt pointer is refused loudly (E1). `builtin://` URIs are accepted as direct read operands.
- **AC2 (no silent empty):** a builtin-resource read that would return an empty payload fails with an error naming the resource id (E5) instead of a silent success.
- **AC3 (bridge loudness):** `bridge_errors.dart` renders `[bridge] GET api.github.com: connection reset (rid c…)` lines — the python HTTP bridge and the curl builtin surface them in the tool result **and** app.log; the bridge makes exactly one attempt (no auto-retry of non-idempotent verbs).
- **AC4 (secret presence):** `SecretsExecutionEnv` injects a names-only roster (`FA_SECRET_VARS`); the sandbox `env` builtin renders `NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT` — values never render; `revokeSecret` keeps the name visible as ABSENT (E3).
- **AC5 (honest timeouts):** bash timeout results render the real cap (never "unknown seconds"), carry the captured partial output, and no longer wear the "uncaught exception" hint; mobile WASI default timeout raised 30s → 120s; killed stages keep a 64 KiB output tail.
- **AC6 (codeload):** the GitHub host matrix (api/raw/codeload/objects.githubusercontent.com + the `curl -L codeload…/tar.gz` recipe) is documented in the mobile host profile (≤1000 chars guard kept); redirect-following curl verified by unit test.
- **AC7 (log hygiene):** normal WASI exit codes log as `_start exited (status N)`, not `_start error:` — error lines in app.log mean harness faults again.
- **AC8 (python noise):** the `Could not find platform dependent libraries` warning is filtered from captured stderr (`WasiPythonNoiseFilter`).
- **E2/E7:** a mid-body connection reset delivers the partial payload with a `[bridge] … after N bytes (truncated)` line and exit 18; responses are capped at 256 MiB with a quota error naming both byte counts (exit 63).

### Key decisions
- Pointer resolution is one pure module (`lib/src/skills/skill_pointer.dart`) shared by the read tool and both mobile shells — one behavior everywhere, unit-testable without WASM.
- `cat` stays a coreutils.wasm applet (the gh-1274/#1335 host-cwd projection is pinned at the WASM stage boundary); the shell dispatches to a Dart cat **only** when a pointer is actually in play (`_catNeedsPointerSeam`: `builtin://` operand, or a missing file whose `.pointer` sibling resolves — an existing file always wins).
- The presence roster rides the exec env (names only) — no new wire, shells stay decorator-agnostic.
- Fixed a self-introduced curl `-w` regression (`%{url_effective}` rendered empty after the loud-failure refactor) by passing the effective URL explicitly.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/tools test/env test/secrets test/agent
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/bridge_loud_failures_test.dart \
  test/builtin_skill_pointer_test.dart test/sandbox_registry_test.dart \
  test/memory_shell_test.dart test/wasm_shell_builtins_test.dart \
  test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart test/sandbox_secret_presence_test.dart \
  test/sandbox_curl_data_test.dart test/wasm_shell_host_cwd_test.dart
```

**Known pre-existing failures in this runner (not from this branch):** golden pixel tests (proven: `origin/main` fails them identically — font rasterization drift), `wasm_sandbox_toolchain_test` (no desktop `libwasm_run_dart.so` provisioned), `providers_queue_writer_io_test` + 6 `test/integration` e2e tests (the runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` env var; all 6 pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`). Simulator-only E2E legs (AC1 byte-identical on device, AC6 real codeload tarball, AC7 app.log spot-check) need an iOS simulator run.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  M[model] -->|read .fah/skills/n/SKILL.md| RT[read tool]
  RT --> SP[skill_pointer resolver]
  SP -->|builtin://skills target| EMB[compiled-in SKILL.md]
  SP -->|foreign target| ERR[loud refusal]
  M -->|bash cat / env| WS[WASI shell]
  WS -->|cat + pointer in play| SEAM[Dart cat seam]
  WS -->|plain cat| APP[coreutils.wasm applet]
  SEAM --> SP
  WS -->|python bridge / curl| BR[bridge_errors lines]
  BR --> TR[tool result stderr] & LOG[app.log bridge tag]
  SE[SecretsExecutionEnv roster] -->|FA_SECRET_VARS| WS
```

</details>

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1453
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1453
- **Title**: gh-1444 [GOAL] iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1444` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 35
- **Additions**: +2775
- **Deletions**: -148
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T14:04:39Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T18:21:25Z

## PR Description

Closes #1444
### What changed
Made the mobile sandbox fail loudly instead of silently (gh-1444): skill reads resolve `.pointer` files transparently, every swallowed network request renders a structured `[bridge]` error, secret presence is verifiable (`NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT`), and timeout results tell the truth.

- **AC1 (pointer reads):** `read .fah/skills/<n>/SKILL.md` follows the sibling `.pointer` to the compiled-in body via a new pure `skill_pointer.dart` resolver — wired into the `read` tool (all hosts), a conditional `cat` seam on the WASI shell, and the web `MemoryShell` file seam. Only `builtin://skills/…` targets resolve; a foreign/corrupt pointer is refused loudly (E1). `builtin://` URIs are accepted as direct read operands.
- **AC2 (no silent empty):** a builtin-resource read that would return an empty payload fails with an error naming the resource id (E5) instead of a silent success.
- **AC3 (bridge loudness):** `bridge_errors.dart` renders `[bridge] GET api.github.com: connection reset (rid c…)` lines — the python HTTP bridge and the curl builtin surface them in the tool result **and** app.log; the bridge makes exactly one attempt (no auto-retry of non-idempotent verbs).
- **AC4 (secret presence):** `SecretsExecutionEnv` injects a names-only roster (`FA_SECRET_VARS`); the sandbox `env` builtin renders `NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT` — values never render; `revokeSecret` keeps the name visible as ABSENT (E3).
- **AC5 (honest timeouts):** bash timeout results render the real cap (never "unknown seconds"), carry the captured partial output, and no longer wear the "uncaught exception" hint; mobile WASI default timeout raised 30s → 120s; killed stages keep a 64 KiB output tail.
- **AC6 (codeload):** the GitHub host matrix (api/raw/codeload/objects.githubusercontent.com + the `curl -L codeload…/tar.gz` recipe) is documented in the mobile host profile (≤1000 chars guard kept); redirect-following curl verified by unit test.
- **AC7 (log hygiene):** normal WASI exit codes log as `_start exited (status N)`, not `_start error:` — error lines in app.log mean harness faults again.
- **AC8 (python noise):** the `Could not find platform dependent libraries` warning is filtered from captured stderr (`WasiPythonNoiseFilter`).
- **E2/E7:** a mid-body connection reset delivers the partial payload with a `[bridge] … after N bytes (truncated)` line and exit 18; responses are capped at 256 MiB with a quota error naming both byte counts (exit 63).

### Key decisions
- Pointer resolution is one pure module (`lib/src/skills/skill_pointer.dart`) shared by the read tool and both mobile shells — one behavior everywhere, unit-testable without WASM.
- `cat` stays a coreutils.wasm applet (the gh-1274/#1335 host-cwd projection is pinned at the WASM stage boundary); the shell dispatches to a Dart cat **only** when a pointer is actually in play (`_catNeedsPointerSeam`: `builtin://` operand, or a missing file whose `.pointer` sibling resolves — an existing file always wins).
- The presence roster rides the exec env (names only) — no new wire, shells stay decorator-agnostic.
- Fixed a self-introduced curl `-w` regression (`%{url_effective}` rendered empty after the loud-failure refactor) by passing the effective URL explicitly.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/tools test/env test/secrets test/agent
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/bridge_loud_failures_test.dart \
  test/builtin_skill_pointer_test.dart test/sandbox_registry_test.dart \
  test/memory_shell_test.dart test/wasm_shell_builtins_test.dart \
  test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart test/sandbox_secret_presence_test.dart \
  test/sandbox_curl_data_test.dart test/wasm_shell_host_cwd_test.dart
```

# pr-1453: gh-1444 [GOAL] iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth

## Description

Closes #1444
### What changed
Made the mobile sandbox fail loudly instead of silently (gh-1444): skill reads resolve `.pointer` files transparently, every swallowed network request renders a structured `[bridge]` error, secret presence is verifiable (`NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT`), and timeout results tell the truth.

- **AC1 (pointer reads):** `read .fah/skills/<n>/SKILL.md` follows the sibling `.pointer` to the compiled-in body via a new pure `skill_pointer.dart` resolver — wired into the `read` tool (all hosts), a conditional `cat` seam on the WASI shell, and the web `MemoryShell` file seam. Only `builtin://skills/…` targets resolve; a foreign/corrupt pointer is refused loudly (E1). `builtin://` URIs are accepted as direct read operands.
- **AC2 (no silent empty):** a builtin-resource read that would return an empty payload fails with an error naming the resource id (E5) instead of a silent success.
- **AC3 (bridge loudness):** `bridge_errors.dart` renders `[bridge] GET api.github.com: connection reset (rid c…)` lines — the python HTTP bridge and the curl builtin surface them in the tool result **and** app.log; the bridge makes exactly one attempt (no auto-retry of non-idempotent verbs).
- **AC4 (secret presence):** `SecretsExecutionEnv` injects a names-only roster (`FA_SECRET_VARS`); the sandbox `env` builtin renders `NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT` — values never render; `revokeSecret` keeps the name visible as ABSENT (E3).
- **AC5 (honest timeouts):** bash timeout results render the real cap (never "unknown seconds"), carry the captured partial output, and no longer wear the "uncaught exception" hint; mobile WASI default timeout raised 30s → 120s; killed stages keep a 64 KiB output tail.
- **AC6 (codeload):** the GitHub host matrix (api/raw/codeload/objects.githubusercontent.com + the `curl -L codeload…/tar.gz` recipe) is documented in the mobile host profile (≤1000 chars guard kept); redirect-following curl verified by unit test.
- **AC7 (log hygiene):** normal WASI exit codes log as `_start exited (status N)`, not `_start error:` — error lines in app.log mean harness faults again.
- **AC8 (python noise):** the `Could not find platform dependent libraries` warning is filtered from captured stderr (`WasiPythonNoiseFilter`).
- **E2/E7:** a mid-body connection reset delivers the partial payload with a `[bridge] … after N bytes (truncated)` line and exit 18; responses are capped at 256 MiB with a quota error naming both byte counts (exit 63).

### Key decisions
- Pointer resolution is one pure module (`lib/src/skills/skill_pointer.dart`) shared by the read tool and both mobile shells — one behavior everywhere, unit-testable without WASM.
- `cat` stays a coreutils.wasm applet (the gh-1274/#1335 host-cwd projection is pinned at the WASM stage boundary); the shell dispatches to a Dart cat **only** when a pointer is actually in play (`_catNeedsPointerSeam`: `builtin://` operand, or a missing file whose `.pointer` sibling resolves — an existing file always wins).
- The presence roster rides the exec env (names only) — no new wire, shells stay decorator-agnostic.
- Fixed a self-introduced curl `-w` regression (`%{url_effective}` rendered empty after the loud-failure refactor) by passing the effective URL explicitly.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/tools test/env test/secrets test/agent
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/bridge_loud_failures_test.dart \
  test/builtin_skill_pointer_test.dart test/sandbox_registry_test.dart \
  test/memory_shell_test.dart test/wasm_shell_builtins_test.dart \
  test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart test/sandbox_secret_presence_test.dart \
  test/sandbox_curl_data_test.dart test/wasm_shell_host_cwd_test.dart
```

**Known pre-existing failures in this runner (not from this branch):** golden pixel tests (proven: `origin/main` fails them identically — font rasterization drift), `wasm_sandbox_toolchain_test` (no desktop `libwasm_run_dart.so` provisioned), `providers_queue_writer_io_test` + 6 `test/integration` e2e tests (the runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` env var; all 6 pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`). Simulator-only E2E legs (AC1 byte-identical on device, AC6 real codeload tarball, AC7 app.log spot-check) need an iOS simulator run.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  M[model] -->|read .fah/skills/n/SKILL.md| RT[read tool]
  RT --> SP[skill_pointer resolver]
  SP -->|builtin://skills target| EMB[compiled-in SKILL.md]
  SP -->|foreign target| ERR[loud refusal]
  M -->|bash cat / env| WS[WASI shell]
  WS -->|cat + pointer in play| SEAM[Dart cat seam]
  WS -->|plain cat| APP[coreutils.wasm applet]
  SEAM --> SP
  WS -->|python bridge / curl| BR[bridge_errors lines]
  BR --> TR[tool result stderr] & LOG[app.log bridge tag]
  SE[SecretsExecutionEnv roster] -->|FA_SECRET_VARS| WS
```

</details>

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1453
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1453
- **Title**: gh-1444 [GOAL] iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1444` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 35
- **Additions**: +2775
- **Deletions**: -148
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T14:04:39Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T18:21:25Z

## PR Description

Closes #1444
### What changed
Made the mobile sandbox fail loudly instead of silently (gh-1444): skill reads resolve `.pointer` files transparently, every swallowed network request renders a structured `[bridge]` error, secret presence is verifiable (`NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT`), and timeout results tell the truth.

- **AC1 (pointer reads):** `read .fah/skills/<n>/SKILL.md` follows the sibling `.pointer` to the compiled-in body via a new pure `skill_pointer.dart` resolver — wired into the `read` tool (all hosts), a conditional `cat` seam on the WASI shell, and the web `MemoryShell` file seam. Only `builtin://skills/…` targets resolve; a foreign/corrupt pointer is refused loudly (E1). `builtin://` URIs are accepted as direct read operands.
- **AC2 (no silent empty):** a builtin-resource read that would return an empty payload fails with an error naming the resource id (E5) instead of a silent success.
- **AC3 (bridge loudness):** `bridge_errors.dart` renders `[bridge] GET api.github.com: connection reset (rid c…)` lines — the python HTTP bridge and the curl builtin surface them in the tool result **and** app.log; the bridge makes exactly one attempt (no auto-retry of non-idempotent verbs).
- **AC4 (secret presence):** `SecretsExecutionEnv` injects a names-only roster (`FA_SECRET_VARS`); the sandbox `env` builtin renders `NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT` — values never render; `revokeSecret` keeps the name visible as ABSENT (E3).
- **AC5 (honest timeouts):** bash timeout results render the real cap (never "unknown seconds"), carry the captured partial output, and no longer wear the "uncaught exception" hint; mobile WASI default timeout raised 30s → 120s; killed stages keep a 64 KiB output tail.
- **AC6 (codeload):** the GitHub host matrix (api/raw/codeload/objects.githubusercontent.com + the `curl -L codeload…/tar.gz` recipe) is documented in the mobile host profile (≤1000 chars guard kept); redirect-following curl verified by unit test.
- **AC7 (log hygiene):** normal WASI exit codes log as `_start exited (status N)`, not `_start error:` — error lines in app.log mean harness faults again.
- **AC8 (python noise):** the `Could not find platform dependent libraries` warning is filtered from captured stderr (`WasiPythonNoiseFilter`).
- **E2/E7:** a mid-body connection reset delivers the partial payload with a `[bridge] … after N bytes (truncated)` line and exit 18; responses are capped at 256 MiB with a quota error naming both byte counts (exit 63).

### Key decisions
- Pointer resolution is one pure module (`lib/src/skills/skill_pointer.dart`) shared by the read tool and both mobile shells — one behavior everywhere, unit-testable without WASM.
- `cat` stays a coreutils.wasm applet (the gh-1274/#1335 host-cwd projection is pinned at the WASM stage boundary); the shell dispatches to a Dart cat **only** when a pointer is actually in play (`_catNeedsPointerSeam`: `builtin://` operand, or a missing file whose `.pointer` sibling resolves — an existing file always wins).
- The presence roster rides the exec env (names only) — no new wire, shells stay decorator-agnostic.
- Fixed a self-introduced curl `-w` regression (`%{url_effective}` rendered empty after the loud-failure refactor) by passing the effective URL explicitly.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/tools test/env test/secrets test/agent
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/bridge_loud_failures_test.dart \
  test/builtin_skill_pointer_test.dart test/sandbox_registry_test.dart \
  test/memory_shell_test.dart test/wasm_shell_builtins_test.dart \
  test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart test/sandbox_secret_presence_test.dart \
  test/sandbox_curl_data_test.dart test/wasm_shell_host_cwd_test.dart
```

**Known pre-existing failures in this runner (not from this branch):** golden pixel tests (proven: `origin/main` fails them identically — font rasterization drift), `wasm_sandbox_toolchain_test` (no desktop `libwasm_run_dart.so` provisioned), `providers_queue_writer_io_test` + 6 `test/integration` e2e tests (the runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` env var; all 6 pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`). Simulator-only E2E legs (AC1 byte-identical on device, AC6 real codeload tarball, AC7 app.log spot-check) need an iOS simulator run.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  M[model] -->|read .fah/skills/n/SKILL.md| RT[read tool]
  RT --> SP[skill_pointer resolver]
  SP -->|builtin://skills target| EMB[compiled-in SKILL.md]
  SP -->|foreign target| ERR[loud refusal]
  M -->|bash cat / env| WS[WASI shell]
  WS -->|cat + pointer in play| SEAM[Dart cat seam]
  WS -->|plain cat| APP[coreutils.wasm applet]
  SEAM --> SP
  WS -->|python bridge / curl| BR[bridge_errors lines]
  BR --> TR[tool result stderr] & LOG[app.log bridge tag]
  SE[SecretsExecutionEnv roster] -->|FA_SECRET_VARS| WS
```

</details>

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 6

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):
🚨 **BLOCKING** — two red CI gates plus a sandbox regression must be fixed before merge.

**Summary**: The PR delivers solid, well-tested work (skill-pointer seam, env secret-presence roster, loud bridge failures, noise filtering — 1267 core tests green locally), but (1) the Quality gate is red: the new `&& timeoutArg != null` guard makes an inner null-check dead code → 2 analyzer warnings (`dart analyze` exit 2 vs 0 on main, reproduced locally); (2) the Flutter app CRAP ratchet is red (new/changed uncovered branches exceed the pinned 30.0 threshold); (3) the new `cat` pointer-seam probe reads every operand with `File.readAsString()`, so `cat` of any binary file (a downloaded tarball/PNG) now throws an uncaught exception where the coreutils applet previously handled it.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 Red CI: Quality gate (analyzer warnings at `builtin_tools_bash.dart:375`) and Flutter app CRAP ratchet (see the workflow's `crap_report.json` artifact for the ranked violators).
- 🚨 `WasiSandboxShell._catNeedsPointerSeam` crashes on non-UTF-8 `cat` operands and double-reads every seamed file.
- ⚠️ AC4's `NAME: ABSENT` half never renders in the app — only granted names are registered, `revokeSecret` has no production caller; the C4 empty-expansion retry loop survives for not-yet-granted names.
- 💡 Desktop `env` still prints raw values (real `/usr/bin/env`) plus the new `FA_SECRET_VARS` names line, while mobile/web render `PRESENT/ABSENT` — a cross-surface divergence to note (no new value leak; roster is names-only).
- 💡 AC6 remains documentation + simulated-client only; the device/simulator leg is deferred (noted in the PR — keep gh-1444's C6 open until it runs).

**Next Steps**:
1. Drop the redundant inner `timeoutArg != null` check (one-line fix) → Quality gate green.
2. Binary-safe the cat probe (bounded `readAsBytes` prefix or `.pointer`-existence gate) + add a binary-`cat` test; re-measure CRAP and cover or descent-note the new branches per `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`.
3. Register the prompt's advertised secret-name roster (or note the limitation) so `env` can render `ABSENT`.

---

### Thread 8

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):
## All three blockers fixed (plus the IMPORTANT and SUGGESTION threads)

**1. Quality gate (analyzer warnings) — fixed.** The redundant inner `timeoutArg != null` check in `lib/src/tools/builtin_tools_bash.dart` (dead code under the new retry guard's promotion) is dropped — exactly the one-line fix proposed. `dart analyze lib test bin` exits 0 again (45 pre-existing info-level hints, 0 warnings/errors).

**2. Binary-`cat` sandbox regression — fixed.** `_catNeedsPointerSeam` no longer reads operands at all: an existence probe keeps every existing file (text OR binary) on the binary-safe coreutils applet path, and only a *missing* operand consults pointer machinery. The Dart `_catBuiltin` (seam path) reads operands byte-first and appends raw bytes, so a tarball beside a pointer seam is delivered instead of thrown out of `exec()`; the text-only `_readSandboxTextFollowPointers` helper is deleted. Covered by the requested flutter unit test (`cat` of a non-UTF-8 tarball through `WasiSandboxShell` — exit 0, never throws; reproduced RED first with the exact `FileSystemException: Failed to decode data using encoding 'utf-8'` this review reported).

**3. CRAP ratchet — re-measured after the cat-probe fix landed** (as the thread required): see the thread-3 reply for the ranked violators and the covering tests / descent outcome.

Also fixed in this round:

- **AC4 `NAME: ABSENT` (IMPORTANT thread):** the roster registers the *advertised* name list (boot values + `knownKeyNames`), and the Keys settings delete is wired as the production `revokeSecret` path (delete → ABSENT with the name visible, re-save → PRESENT; dotenv-only names untouched). Five new `AgentService.create`-level tests pin it.
- **IPv6 `bridgeHostOfAuthority` (SUGGESTION):** now parses through `Uri` (`http://[::1]:8080/x` → `::1`), with tests; a corrupt authority still renders instead of crashing the failure path.

**Noted, no action (as flagged):** desktop CLI `env` keeps printing raw values (real `/usr/bin/env`) next to the names-only roster line — cross-surface divergence, no new value leak; AC6's device/simulator leg (real codeload tarball) stays deferred with gh-1444's C6 open until it runs.

---


## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

🚨 **BLOCKING: New analyzer warnings — `dart analyze` gate is red**

Adding `&& timeoutArg != null` to the retry guard promotes `timeoutArg` to non-null inside the block, which turns the pre-existing interpolation check below into dead code:

```dart
if (error.code == ExecutionErrorCode.timeout &&
    canRetry &&
    timeoutArg != null) {          // <- promotion happens here
  notices.add(
    '[bash attempt ... timed out'
    '${timeoutArg != null ? ' after ${timeoutArg}s' : ''} — '   // <- always true → warning + dead `: ''` branch
```

Reproduced locally: `dart analyze lib test bin` exits **2** on this branch (2 warnings: `unnecessary_null_comparison` + `dead_code` at `builtin_tools_bash.dart:375`) vs exit **0** on `origin/main`. This is the root cause of the failing **Quality gate** CI check.

Fix — the inner check is redundant under the new guard:

```dart
'[bash attempt $attempt/${bashToolMaxRetries + 1} timed out'
' after ${timeoutArg}s — '
'retrying]',
```

(The `throw _bashFailureError(error, notices, timeoutArg)` below is outside the guard and correctly still handles null.)

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `cat` of a binary file now throws an uncaught exception (mobile sandbox regression)**

`_catNeedsPointerSeam` eagerly calls `_readSandboxText(path)` — a full `File.readAsString()` — for **every** non-flag operand of **every** `cat` invocation, before the coreutils applet runs:

```dart
for (final path in args.where((a) => !a.startsWith('-'))) {
  if (await _readSandboxText(path) != null) continue;
```

`readAsString()` throws (`FileSystemException: Failed to decode data using encoding 'utf-8'`) on any non-UTF-8 content — a downloaded tarball, PNG, gzip blob. That exception escapes `_runStage` → `runShellScript` → `exec()`. The `Shell` contract returns `Result`, callers don't expect throws, so the tool surfaces an "uncaught exception inside the harness" error for a command that worked before this PR (the coreutils.wasm applet is binary-safe). This is exactly the file class AC6's own recipe produces (`curl -L ... codeload.github.com/.../tar.gz/...`).

Two additional costs even for valid text: every seamed `cat` reads the file **twice** (probe + applet), and the probe reads the *whole* file just to check for a pointer.

Suggested fix:

1. Probe cheaply and binary-safely: read a bounded prefix via `file.readAsBytes()` (e.g. first 4 KiB), treat `utf8.decode(prefix, allowMalformed: true)` losslessness (or a NUL-byte sniff) as the text test — or gate the probe on the existence of a `<path>.pointer` sibling via `File.exists()` instead of reading the operand at all.
2. Decide the binary path deliberately: with no pointer, let the applet handle the operand (pre-PR behavior) instead of routing bytes through a UTF-8 text API — both here and in `_catBuiltin`'s `_readSandboxTextFollowPointers` fallback, which has the same throw on binary operands.

Please add a flutter unit test: `cat` of a non-UTF-8 file through `WasiSandboxShell` returns the bytes/exit 0 and never throws.

# pr-1453: gh-1444 [GOAL] iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth

## Description

Closes #1444
### What changed
Made the mobile sandbox fail loudly instead of silently (gh-1444): skill reads resolve `.pointer` files transparently, every swallowed network request renders a structured `[bridge]` error, secret presence is verifiable (`NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT`), and timeout results tell the truth.

- **AC1 (pointer reads):** `read .fah/skills/<n>/SKILL.md` follows the sibling `.pointer` to the compiled-in body via a new pure `skill_pointer.dart` resolver — wired into the `read` tool (all hosts), a conditional `cat` seam on the WASI shell, and the web `MemoryShell` file seam. Only `builtin://skills/…` targets resolve; a foreign/corrupt pointer is refused loudly (E1). `builtin://` URIs are accepted as direct read operands.
- **AC2 (no silent empty):** a builtin-resource read that would return an empty payload fails with an error naming the resource id (E5) instead of a silent success.
- **AC3 (bridge loudness):** `bridge_errors.dart` renders `[bridge] GET api.github.com: connection reset (rid c…)` lines — the python HTTP bridge and the curl builtin surface them in the tool result **and** app.log; the bridge makes exactly one attempt (no auto-retry of non-idempotent verbs).
- **AC4 (secret presence):** `SecretsExecutionEnv` injects a names-only roster (`FA_SECRET_VARS`); the sandbox `env` builtin renders `NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT` — values never render; `revokeSecret` keeps the name visible as ABSENT (E3).
- **AC5 (honest timeouts):** bash timeout results render the real cap (never "unknown seconds"), carry the captured partial output, and no longer wear the "uncaught exception" hint; mobile WASI default timeout raised 30s → 120s; killed stages keep a 64 KiB output tail.
- **AC6 (codeload):** the GitHub host matrix (api/raw/codeload/objects.githubusercontent.com + the `curl -L codeload…/tar.gz` recipe) is documented in the mobile host profile (≤1000 chars guard kept); redirect-following curl verified by unit test.
- **AC7 (log hygiene):** normal WASI exit codes log as `_start exited (status N)`, not `_start error:` — error lines in app.log mean harness faults again.
- **AC8 (python noise):** the `Could not find platform dependent libraries` warning is filtered from captured stderr (`WasiPythonNoiseFilter`).
- **E2/E7:** a mid-body connection reset delivers the partial payload with a `[bridge] … after N bytes (truncated)` line and exit 18; responses are capped at 256 MiB with a quota error naming both byte counts (exit 63).

### Key decisions
- Pointer resolution is one pure module (`lib/src/skills/skill_pointer.dart`) shared by the read tool and both mobile shells — one behavior everywhere, unit-testable without WASM.
- `cat` stays a coreutils.wasm applet (the gh-1274/#1335 host-cwd projection is pinned at the WASM stage boundary); the shell dispatches to a Dart cat **only** when a pointer is actually in play (`_catNeedsPointerSeam`: `builtin://` operand, or a missing file whose `.pointer` sibling resolves — an existing file always wins).
- The presence roster rides the exec env (names only) — no new wire, shells stay decorator-agnostic.
- Fixed a self-introduced curl `-w` regression (`%{url_effective}` rendered empty after the loud-failure refactor) by passing the effective URL explicitly.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/tools test/env test/secrets test/agent
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/bridge_loud_failures_test.dart \
  test/builtin_skill_pointer_test.dart test/sandbox_registry_test.dart \
  test/memory_shell_test.dart test/wasm_shell_builtins_test.dart \
  test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart test/sandbox_secret_presence_test.dart \
  test/sandbox_curl_data_test.dart test/wasm_shell_host_cwd_test.dart
```

**Known pre-existing failures in this runner (not from this branch):** golden pixel tests (proven: `origin/main` fails them identically — font rasterization drift), `wasm_sandbox_toolchain_test` (no desktop `libwasm_run_dart.so` provisioned), `providers_queue_writer_io_test` + 6 `test/integration` e2e tests (the runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` env var; all 6 pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`). Simulator-only E2E legs (AC1 byte-identical on device, AC6 real codeload tarball, AC7 app.log spot-check) need an iOS simulator run.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  M[model] -->|read .fah/skills/n/SKILL.md| RT[read tool]
  RT --> SP[skill_pointer resolver]
  SP -->|builtin://skills target| EMB[compiled-in SKILL.md]
  SP -->|foreign target| ERR[loud refusal]
  M -->|bash cat / env| WS[WASI shell]
  WS -->|cat + pointer in play| SEAM[Dart cat seam]
  WS -->|plain cat| APP[coreutils.wasm applet]
  SEAM --> SP
  WS -->|python bridge / curl| BR[bridge_errors lines]
  BR --> TR[tool result stderr] & LOG[app.log bridge tag]
  SE[SecretsExecutionEnv roster] -->|FA_SECRET_VARS| WS
```

</details>

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1453
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1453
- **Title**: gh-1444 [GOAL] iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1444` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 35
- **Additions**: +2775
- **Deletions**: -148
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T14:04:39Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T18:21:25Z

## PR Description

Closes #1444
### What changed
Made the mobile sandbox fail loudly instead of silently (gh-1444): skill reads resolve `.pointer` files transparently, every swallowed network request renders a structured `[bridge]` error, secret presence is verifiable (`NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT`), and timeout results tell the truth.

- **AC1 (pointer reads):** `read .fah/skills/<n>/SKILL.md` follows the sibling `.pointer` to the compiled-in body via a new pure `skill_pointer.dart` resolver — wired into the `read` tool (all hosts), a conditional `cat` seam on the WASI shell, and the web `MemoryShell` file seam. Only `builtin://skills/…` targets resolve; a foreign/corrupt pointer is refused loudly (E1). `builtin://` URIs are accepted as direct read operands.
- **AC2 (no silent empty):** a builtin-resource read that would return an empty payload fails with an error naming the resource id (E5) instead of a silent success.
- **AC3 (bridge loudness):** `bridge_errors.dart` renders `[bridge] GET api.github.com: connection reset (rid c…)` lines — the python HTTP bridge and the curl builtin surface them in the tool result **and** app.log; the bridge makes exactly one attempt (no auto-retry of non-idempotent verbs).
- **AC4 (secret presence):** `SecretsExecutionEnv` injects a names-only roster (`FA_SECRET_VARS`); the sandbox `env` builtin renders `NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT` — values never render; `revokeSecret` keeps the name visible as ABSENT (E3).
- **AC5 (honest timeouts):** bash timeout results render the real cap (never "unknown seconds"), carry the captured partial output, and no longer wear the "uncaught exception" hint; mobile WASI default timeout raised 30s → 120s; killed stages keep a 64 KiB output tail.
- **AC6 (codeload):** the GitHub host matrix (api/raw/codeload/objects.githubusercontent.com + the `curl -L codeload…/tar.gz` recipe) is documented in the mobile host profile (≤1000 chars guard kept); redirect-following curl verified by unit test.
- **AC7 (log hygiene):** normal WASI exit codes log as `_start exited (status N)`, not `_start error:` — error lines in app.log mean harness faults again.
- **AC8 (python noise):** the `Could not find platform dependent libraries` warning is filtered from captured stderr (`WasiPythonNoiseFilter`).
- **E2/E7:** a mid-body connection reset delivers the partial payload with a `[bridge] … after N bytes (truncated)` line and exit 18; responses are capped at 256 MiB with a quota error naming both byte counts (exit 63).

### Key decisions
- Pointer resolution is one pure module (`lib/src/skills/skill_pointer.dart`) shared by the read tool and both mobile shells — one behavior everywhere, unit-testable without WASM.
- `cat` stays a coreutils.wasm applet (the gh-1274/#1335 host-cwd projection is pinned at the WASM stage boundary); the shell dispatches to a Dart cat **only** when a pointer is actually in play (`_catNeedsPointerSeam`: `builtin://` operand, or a missing file whose `.pointer` sibling resolves — an existing file always wins).
- The presence roster rides the exec env (names only) — no new wire, shells stay decorator-agnostic.
- Fixed a self-introduced curl `-w` regression (`%{url_effective}` rendered empty after the loud-failure refactor) by passing the effective URL explicitly.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/tools test/env test/secrets test/agent
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/bridge_loud_failures_test.dart \
  test/builtin_skill_pointer_test.dart test/sandbox_registry_test.dart \
  test/memory_shell_test.dart test/wasm_shell_builtins_test.dart \
  test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart test/sandbox_secret_presence_test.dart \
  test/sandbox_curl_data_test.dart test/wasm_shell_host_cwd_test.dart
```

**Known pre-existing failures in this runner (not from this branch):** golden pixel tests (proven: `origin/main` fails them identically — font rasterization drift), `wasm_sandbox_toolchain_test` (no desktop `libwasm_run_dart.so` provisioned), `providers_queue_writer_io_test` + 6 `test/integration` e2e tests (the runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` env var; all 6 pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`). Simulator-only E2E legs (AC1 byte-identical on device, AC6 real codeload tarball, AC7 app.log spot-check) need an iOS simulator run.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  M[model] -->|read .fah/skills/n/SKILL.md| RT[read tool]
  RT --> SP[skill_pointer resolver]
  SP -->|builtin://skills target| EMB[compiled-in SKILL.md]
  SP -->|foreign target| ERR[loud refusal]
  M -->|bash cat / env| WS[WASI shell]
  WS -->|cat + pointer in play| SEAM[Dart cat seam]
  WS -->|plain cat| APP[coreutils.wasm applet]
  SEAM --> SP
  WS -->|python bridge / curl| BR[bridge_errors lines]
  BR --> TR[tool result stderr] & LOG[app.log bridge tag]
  SE[SecretsExecutionEnv roster] -->|FA_SECRET_VARS| WS
```

</details>

**Next Steps**:

2. Binary-safe the cat probe (bounded `readAsBytes` prefix or `.pointer`-existence gate) + add a binary-`cat` test; re-measure CRAP and cover or descent-note the new branches per `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`.

**1. Quality gate (analyzer warnings) — fixed.** The redundant inner `timeoutArg != null` check in `lib/src/tools/builtin_tools_bash.dart` (dead code under the new retry guard's promotion) is dropped — exactly the one-line fix proposed. `dart analyze lib test bin` exits 0 again (45 pre-existing info-level hints, 0 warnings/errors).
